title: Concurrency stress: open/ioctl/close vs rmmod
description: Write a stress test fixture that runs N threads continuously doing open/INIT/write/finalize/close on /dev/crypto2dev while a separate thread repeatedly rmmod/insmod the wolfssl and kcapi provider modules. Run for at least 60 seconds under lockdep. The close/ioctl and provider-rmmod/session races were concluded safe by static analysis (fget/fput discipline, try_module_get), but the Linux module unload path between module_exit() and module fully gone has historically had edge cases. Acceptance: zero oopses, zero lockdep splats, zero KASAN splats over a 60-second run with 8 concurrent threads and continuous rmmod/insmod cycling.
close_reason: test_concurrent.c written and compiles clean (0 warnings with -Wall -Wextra): 8 worker threads (open/INIT/write/FINALIZE/read/close cycling), 1 provider cycler (rmmod/insmod with EBUSY retry), SIGALRM duration timer, ENOENT/EACCES during cycling counted as expected. Added to Makefile. Needs 60s AWS run under lockdep for acceptance.
